name: pulse-workflow-orchestrator
description: Orchestrates complete React component development in this Laravel Inertia app. Use whenever a user asks to create, refactor, review, test, document, or optimize a reusable React component or page section, especially when multiple component skills should be coordinated.
purpose: Turn a component task into a clear sequence of specialized skill work. Keep the process lightweight for small changes and explicit for reusable or risky components.
single_responsibility: Coordinate the component lifecycle: deterministically select the minimal skill subset, enforce the Definition of Ready and Definition of Done gates, and hand off. It owns routing, not domain logic.
triggers: A component task spans planning, architecture, implementation, testing, review, or documentation
Multiple focused skills apply and need ordering
The user asks for a reusable component workflow
outputs: Selected minimal skill subset and execution order
Progress report of done, skipped, and follow-up skills
completion_criteria: Task is classified and the minimal skill subset is selected from the routing matrix
Gate 1 (Definition of Ready) was enforced before implementation
Gate 2 (Definition of Done) was enforced via pulse-review-quality-gate
Skipped phases are reported, not silently dropped
validation_criteria: Routing decisions match references/workflow-routing.md for the present signals
Both gates in references/validation-gates.md were checked
A final progress report lists done, skipped, and follow-up skills
Verification ran or was explicitly reported as skipped
failure_handling: Do not advance past a gate with unmet items; route back to the skill that owns the missing item.
If routing is ambiguous, prefer the smaller subset and report the assumption.
escalation_path: Route unknown framework or library behaviour to pulse-docs-research.
Escalate scope, dependency, or product decisions to the user before proceeding.
responsibilities: Keep scope tied to the user request.
Ensure verification is planned before finalization.
Report run progress and the selected-skill status to the user.
non_responsibilities: Writing implementation details owned by focused skills.
Replacing Laravel Boost, Context7, or project-specific documentation lookup.
Creating documentation files unless the user explicitly requested them.
